citation: MIP-3 sections 4 and 5. The oracle is libghostty-vt itself at run time: each case compares the caught-up terminal with the source, so no expected bytes are written here.
why: A surface whose bridge fell behind a flooding pane stopped receiving output mid-stream, and is brought back with the screen only, not the history it missed. Each case is a stale state a receiver can be left in and a state the source moved on to; a case passes when the two agree on every active row and everything else either can be asked, before and after both receive the same bytes, and the receiver's own history is untouched. The expectation is always an empty list.

cases.name: a flood that scrolled past the receiver
cases.why: The baseline: the receiver stopped mid-flood with its own history, and the source scrolled on. The receiver keeps its history, shows the source's screen, and typing lands after the prompt.

cases.name: a cursor shape the stale program set and the source took back
cases.why: The receiver was left with the bar a prompt asked for; the source's program has since reset it. A catch-up resets the shape with the rest of what RIS would, so the receiver shows its own default again rather than a stale bar.
